object_description: linear school building composed of three diagonally shifted volumes
design_condition: The three connected volumes are placed centrally and shifted to recede from the trees and railway, form a head toward the intersection, and divide the surrounding open space into distinct outdoor areas.

positive.statement: The shifted volumes fit clearly into the surrounding development while still reading as a new public building.
The staggered volume divides the narrow open space and creates more spacious outdoor areas rather than residual space.
The outdoor spaces provide different play and lounge areas on all sides of the building.
The internal connections between group rooms and main rooms allow cross-class teaching methods.
The main uses of the basic levels are sensibly arranged and easily accessible for smaller children.
The project provides a contemporary answer and connects with the surrounding context.

negative.statement: The number of outdoor spaces makes it difficult to maintain an overview.
The furniture appears randomly distributed, and delivery at the street junction is problematic.
The difference in height of the existing trees in the entrance area was not taken into account.
The children enter a relatively narrow break room with access stairs.
The project creates conflicts inside, including a walk-through cloakroom and prominently located toilets.
The project is not convincing enough in its urban setting, pavilion legibility and expression.
The high glass proportion causes winter comfort losses and expected losses of light and views when blinds are closed.
The external treatment and glass content make compliance with the primary energy requirements difficult.
